title: Vertex and Intercepts of a Transformed Absolute Value Graph
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find the vertex, axis of symmetry, and x-intercepts of the transformed absolute value function f(x) = -3|x - 2| + 4.

steps.title: Identify the Vertex via Translations
steps.explanation: The parent absolute value graph y = |x| has its vertex at (0,0). The horizontal shift h = 2 and vertical shift k = 4 translate the vertex to (2, 4). Since a = -3 < 0, the V-shape opens downward.
steps.why: Standard vertex form of an absolute value function places the peak or trough at (h, k).

steps.title: Find the Axis of Symmetry
steps.explanation: Absolute value functions are symmetric about the vertical line passing through their vertex.
steps.why: Reflection symmetry of |x - h| across the vertical line x = h.

steps.title: Calculate the x-Intercepts
steps.explanation: Set f(x) = 0 and isolate the absolute value term to solve for the intersection points with the horizontal axis.
steps.why: The x-intercepts correspond precisely to the real roots of the equation f(x) = 0.

steps.title: Solve the Absolute Value Equation
steps.explanation: Splitting |u| = c into u = c and u = -c yields two distinct symmetric x-intercepts equidistant from the axis of symmetry x = 2.
steps.why: Definition of absolute value as distance on the real coordinate line.
